title: banking_knowledge v1.0.1 — upstream scorer vs revised verified scorer
intro: Two independent reviews of the same 97 tasks on 2026-10-13 with the same model (claude-opus-5-5, effort high), task batches, inputs, verification and calibration prompts. The DB scorer differs: upstream exact-hash grading against the revised verified scorer (extra discoverable calls allowed only when every call was rejected for bad input; closure_reason ignored on bank accounts only). The verified-scorer run also used a later review prompt that adds grading facts confirmed during the upstream run and points reviewers to the calibration file. Both sides show their reviewers' and verifiers' own severities, with no reconciliation, so a difference can come from the scorer, the prompt update, or run-to-run judgment. 'Repeat' is an earlier same-scorer upstream review (draft-1) that shows how much reviewers alone vary.
notes: The upstream side uses that run's reviewer and verifier severities (Blocker 14, Major 35, Minor 21, None 27). Its published report shows severities reconciled against the earlier, superseded verified-scorer run (11 / 40 / 25 / 21); that reconciliation is not used here.

Four differences come from the scorer: 060, 061, 062 and 067 close a bank account, and only the verified scorer ignores a custom closure_reason there. The verified-scorer reviewers and verifiers report that no other verdict in their run depends on the scorer's relaxations, so the remaining 22 differences are differences in judgment or in what each review found, about as many as the 27 between two same-scorer reviews.

The verified-scorer run's review prompt adds grading facts confirmed during the upstream run (read log keyed by tool name, which rejected calls are logged, ACTION grading ignores who made the call, NL assertions multiply into the reward) and points reviewers to calibration.md.
